entries.title: The impact of social media use on appearance anxiety among college students —the chain mediating effect of upward social comparison and envy
entries.abstract: Background The widespread adoption of digital media has reshaped young people’s aesthetic experiences. The abundance of idealized and digitally enhanced appearance-related content on social media has made appearance anxiety increasingly prevalent among university students. However, the psychological pathways linking social media use to appearance anxiety require systematic examination. This study examined the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety among university students and tested the chain mediating roles of upward social comparison and envy. Methods Using convenience sampling, 1,640 university students in China completed the Social Media Use Intensity Scale, Appearance Anxiety Scale, Upward Social Comparison Scale, and Envy Scale. Confirmatory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and PROCESS Model 6 analysis with 5,000 percentile bootstrap samples were used to examine the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety and the chain mediating effects of upward social comparison and envy. All regression equations controlled for gender, educational level, and average daily social media use time. Results (1) Social media use was significantly and positively associated with appearance anxiety among university students. (2) Upward social comparison mediated the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety. (3) Envy mediated the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety. (4) Upward social comparison and envy showed a significant chain mediating effect in the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety. Conclusion This study provided preliminary cross-sectional evidence for an appearance-anxiety-specific comparison–envy pattern linking social media use to appearance anxiety among university students. The findings provide theoretical and practical implications for aesthetic education and media literacy education in higher education within the digital media environment. They may also help guide university students toward more rational aesthetic perceptions, reduced appearance anxiety, and improved physical and mental well-being.

entries.title: Mindful Awareness as a Mediator Between Social Appearance Anxiety and Social Media Addiction in Adolescents
entries.venue: Journal of Psychosocial Nursing and Mental Health Services
entries.abstract: PURPOSE: Adolescence is a critical period for identity formation and social development, and social media can shape appearance perceptions and social acceptance. Social appearance anxiety may be associated with greater vulnerability to social media addiction, whereas mindful awareness may be linked to lower levels of this risk. The current study tested mindful awareness as a mediator between social appearance anxiety and social media addiction in adolescents. METHOD: The sample comprised 383 volunteer secondary school students in eastern Türkiye during the 2024-2025 academic year. Participants completed standardized measures of social appearance anxiety, mindful awareness, and social media addiction. RESULTS: Social appearance anxiety was positively related to social media addiction and negatively related to mindful awareness; mindful awareness was also negatively related to addiction. CONCLUSION: Mediation results indicated partial mediation, suggesting mindfulness-based interventions may reduce appearance anxiety and promote healthier social media use among adolescents. Findings highlight mindful awareness as a target for prevention.
